### Before you start

By [the start of this week's Wednesday lecture]{style="color:#bb0000"},
you should make sure you have access to a personal GitHub account.
For most of you, that will mean you need to create an account, as detailed below.

GitHub is a website that hosts *Git repositories*, i.e. version-controlled projects.
In this week of the course, you'll learn how to use Git together with GitHub.

### Detailed steps

*If you already have a GitHub account, [log in](https://github.com/) and start at step 6.*

1. Go to <https://github.com>.

2. Click the "Sign Up" button all the way in the top right corner of the page.

3. Fill out the form (don't use "Continue with Google") to provide your personal
   details -- some notes:
  
   - When choosing your **_username_**, I recommend to
     *keep it professional and make it include or resemble your real name*.
     (Keep in mind that you may use GitHub to share your code,
     like when publishing a paper.)
  
   - It's up to you whether you prefer to use your OSU email address
     or a non-institutional **_email address_** --
     _but is should match the email address in your_
     [_Git configuration_](/week05/w5a_git.qmd#one-time-git-configuration)
     (Also note that you can always associate a second email address with your
     account.).

5. Check your email and click the link to **_verify your email address_**.

:::: columns
::: {.column width="85%"}

6. You should now be back on the GitHub website, logged in.
   In the far top-right corner of the page,
   click your randomly assigned "avatar" (see image on right),
   and in the dropdown menu, click "Settings".

:::
::: {.column width="15%"}
![](../img/github-avatar.png){width="40%" fig-align="center"}
:::

::::

7. In the "Public profile" tab, enter your name.

8. _Optional:_ Still in the "Profile tab", upload a Profile picture.
   This can be a picture of yourself but if you prefer, you can use something else.
   
9. Send your GitHub username to Jelmer.
